title: Five Nights at Freddy's
summary: A night guard, Mike Schmidt, works a week at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza while its four machines roam at night. A recorded voice on the phone guides him and speaks of the Bite of '87, and rare newspaper clippings report children lured into a back room and never found.
settingYearLabel: A November after 1987 (the cheques print a day and a month, and no year)

title: Five Nights at Freddy's 2
summary: A night guard, Jeremy Fitzgerald, works the last week of a new Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, among new machines and four older ones kept for parts. The phone calls report an investigation, a lockdown and a spare yellow suit that someone used. Minigames that can follow a death show a purple figure killing a child who cries outside, and the Puppet giving masks to four grey, dead-looking children.

title: Five Nights at Freddy's 3
summary: A guard works at Fazbear's Fright, a local amusement park's horror attraction stocked with relics of the old pizzeria. Its builders find one animatronic, a decayed rabbit with what looks like a body inside it. Minigames between the nights show a purple figure taking the four old machines apart and dying inside a yellow rabbit suit.
settingYearLabel: Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed (Scott's store text; no year)

title: Five Nights at Freddy's 4
summary: The player defends a bedroom at night against monstrous versions of the Fazbear characters. Minigames between the nights count down five days to a small boy's birthday party, where Fredbear's jaws close on his head. The game ends on a locked box.
settingYearLabel: c. 1983 (the year on a television show's title card)

title: Five Nights at Freddy's 4: Halloween Edition
summary: A seasonal edition of FNaF4 with changed characters and redecorated minigames. Scott ruled it non-canon.

title: FNaF World
summary: A comic role-playing game with the series' characters as its party. Its adventure is outside the story; its opening words end on FNaF4's promise, "I will put you back together.", and with its clock ending they are used only as support.
settingYearLabel: Outside the story, except its opening and clock-ending text

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Sister Location
summary: A technician works five nights in Circus Baby's Entertainment and Rental, an underground facility marked Afton Robotics whose machines are hired out for parties. Circus Baby guides him to the scooping room. Cutscenes unlocked in its Custom Night show what became of him, and end with a son's speech to his father.
settingYearLabel: Undated; after a Freddy Fazbear's Pizza had closed

title: Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator
summary: A franchisee runs a new pizzeria for one week and is offered wrecked machines to salvage. The restaurant is a trap: the Cassette Man calls four haunted machines into one building and, in the ending that the later games follow, stays as it burns.
settingYearLabel: After the Fazbear's Fright fire, most likely (no year)

title: Ultimate Custom Night
summary: A custom night with fifty selectable characters from the earlier games. Their voices say that the one in the office has killed and cannot die, and one voice says it will hold that person there: "No matter how many times they burn us."
settingYearLabel: After the Pizzeria Simulator fire, most likely (no year)

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted
summary: A virtual-reality game presented as Fazbear Entertainment's own product, the Freddy Fazbear Virtual Experience, which restages the earlier games as fiction. Hidden tapes left by a tester describe something that came into its code from scanned circuit boards.
settingYearLabel: Undated; after the Pizzeria Simulator fire by convention

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted - Curse of Dreadbear
summary: A Halloween add-on to Help Wanted: new levels in the same virtual product. With a hidden rabbit mask on, and the plush from Help Wanted's Trapped ending in hand, the player hears a woman's side of a conversation with someone who is never heard.

title: Five Nights at Freddy's AR: Special Delivery
summary: An augmented-reality mobile game in which the Fazbear Funtime Service delivers the company's machines to its subscribers. Company emails that reach the player tell of a contractor's scan of old circuit boards that released a virus, and of an employee whose searches alarm a colleague.
settingYearLabel: Undated; its emails count only in their order

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach
summary: A boy, Gregory, spends one night inside Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex. Glamrock Freddy helps him against the other machines, the guard Vanessa and a woman in a rabbit costume. The game has six endings, one of which goes down to a pizzeria buried under the building.

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach - RUIN
summary: An add-on to Security Breach. Cassie goes into the wrecked Pizzaplex to find Gregory, led by a voice that uses his words, and switches off the security system that was keeping something sealed underneath.

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted 2
summary: A staff training program of tasks in the Mega Pizzaplex, seen through a mask; with the mask off, its bright hub is a dark, derelict room. In its main ending, as a fan wiki describes it, a large box on the hub's stage opens on a recharge station, and a robot holds a rabbit mask out to a girl.
settingYearLabel: Most likely between Security Breach's night and RUIN

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit
summary: An adventure game, and an adaptation that the main games never place. A boy, Oswald, climbs into a ball pit at a run-down pizzeria and comes out in an older Freddy Fazbear's Pizza; in the present, a yellow rabbit pulls his father into the pit.
settingYearLabel: Not placed; a logo graphic reads 1985, which dates nothing

title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Secret of the Mimic
summary: Fazbear Entertainment sends a technician by night into the shuttered workshop of Murray's Costume Manor to bring out its blueprints. An endoskeleton is loose in the building, and earlier visitors lie dead inside mascot costumes. Recordings and letters tell the story of Edwin Murray, his family and his two machines.
settingYearLabel: 1979, most likely 7 September (on a work order read from an image, not yet seen in play)

title: Freddy in Space 2
summary: A comic side-scrolling shooter spin-off. The archive holds no records from it, and it is outside the story.
